Answer: A
Reason: The initial chest X-ray (Figure 1a) shows a large left-sided mediastinal mass with significant opacity and mediastinal shift to the left, indicating volume loss/collapse. The post-treatment X-ray (Figure 1b) demonstrates resolution of the mass, normalization of the mediastinal position (shift resolved), and clear lung fields indicating re-expansion. Option A is the only choice that correctly identifies the decrease in mass size and the associated improvement in mediastinal shift and lung expansion.
